study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier provided in paper.

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.
target_condition.notes: Primary condition investigated throughout the study.

control.notes: Study_level granularity: paper contains both cases and controls but no per-sample control designation provided.

country.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples, respectively
body_site.notes: Primary body site for microbiota analysis was feces.

body_site_details.evidence_quote: Stools were collected according to International Human Microbiome Standards (IHMS)
body_site_details.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction

days_from_first_collection.notes: Cross-sectional study; no longitudinal timepoints reported.

lifestyle.notes: Not applicable; study is from westernized population.

location.evidence_quote: three specialized centres in Denmark: Center for Eating Disorders (Odense University Hospital), Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Unit (Aarhus University Hospital) and Unit for Psychiatric Research (Aalborg University Hospital).

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; periodontal measurements not part of this study.

westernized.notes: Inferred from context: study population is Danish/European, classified as westernized.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

probing_pocket_depth_value.notes: Not applicable; periodontal measurements not part of this study.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2, using NucleoSpin soil mini kit (MACHEREY-NAGEL).
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: MACHEREY-NAGEL manufactures the NucleoSpin kit; maps to NorgenBiotek family in allowed values.

ncbi_accession.notes: No NCBI SRA/ENA accessions explicitly cited in the paper text.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)
sequencing_platform.notes: Ion Proton platform used for human sample shotgun sequencing.

age.notes: Study-level age not reported; only age-matched cohorts mentioned. Animal experiments used 6-week-old female mice.

age_group.evidence_quote: 77 female AN cases and 70 healthy females
age_group.notes: Inferred: EDI-3 is designed for females aged 13-53; context indicates adult women.

age_unit.notes: Inferred from standard clinical reporting convention.

ancestry.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women

family.notes: Not applicable; individual recruitment, not family-based sampling.

family_role.notes: Not applicable; family-based sampling not used.

sex.evidence_quote: Since 90–95% of individuals with diagnosed AN are females, we decided to include only women
sex.notes: All human study participants were female.

age_min.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_min.notes: Inferred from EDI-3 age range used for study participants; actual study participants' age range not explicitly stated in abstract or methods overview.

age_max.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_max.notes: Inferred from EDI-3 age range; actual study participants' age not specified in detail.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Participants with recent antibiotic use within 3 months were excluded from the study.

disease.evidence_quote: The AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and they met the DSM-5 criteria for the restricting or binge/purging subtypes of AN.
disease.notes: Study includes AN cases and healthy controls; AN cases stratified into AN-RS and AN-BP subtypes.

disease_details.evidence_quote: It can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type.
disease_details.notes: AN patients classified into two subtypes based on DSM-5 criteria.

bmi.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from randomly selected subsets of three patients with AN (females aged 20, 22 and 20 yr with BMI of 10.3, 11.5 and 11.7 kg m−2, respectively) and three HC (females aged 20, 22 and 21 yr with BMI of 22.6, 21.1 and 21.2 kg m−2, respectively)
bmi.notes: Values are from FMT donor cohort; calculated mean BMI for AN donors = (10.3+11.5+11.7)/3 = 11.5; mean BMI for HC donors = (22.6+21.1+21.2)/3 = 21.6.

smoker.evidence_quote: Differential analysis...where covariates including age, BMI, smoking and medication...were corrected.
smoker.notes: Smoking status was used as a covariate in analyses but specific prevalence or distribution not reported in main text or abstract.

treatment.evidence_quote: Species that were significantly different...after deconfounding interferences of multiple medications (selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines)
treatment.notes: These medications were used as confounding variables; specific medication usage rates not detailed. Healthy controls excluded if taking regular medication apart from birth control pills.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: The exclusion criteria for the age-matched healthy control women were BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg m−1−2, regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pills were permitted in healthy controls but other regular medications were exclusion criteria.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Multiple bacterial taxa (for example, Clostridium species) were altered in AN and correlated with estimates of eating behaviour and mental health.
biomarker_name.notes: List compiled from multiple sections including Abstract, Results, and metabolomics findings. Biomarkers represent bacterial taxa, viral species, and serum metabolites measured in the study.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples, respectively, from a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females.
biomarker_unit.notes: Units inferred from methodology; specific quantitative units not uniformly reported across all biomarkers in the paper.

biomarker_value.notes: Paper reports differential abundance and associations rather than absolute values for most biomarkers. Specific numerical biomarker values are presented in figures and tables but not in a unified summary format suitable for extraction.

disease_response_os.notes: This is an observational cross-sectional study of AN pathogenesis, not a treatment trial. No overall survival data or follow-up duration is reported.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; no survival data provided.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status is not reported in this AN microbiome study. The paper focuses on microbiota composition and metabolites, not performance status.

value: altered bacterial composition at phylum level
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: At the phylum level, AN microbiota samples were characterized by a reduction in Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota. We observed higher β-diversity of AN microbiome at the genus level.
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes documented through shotgun metagenomics. No significant difference in bacterial cell counts between AN and HC (P Wilcoxon > 0.05, Supplementary Table 1).

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this is an AN microbiome study, not an oncology study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor measurements relevant to this AN pathogenesis study.

value: Cohort: 77 females with AN, 70 healthy female controls, age-matched
Study location: Denmark; Danish Caucasian women only
Exclusion criteria: antibiotic/antifungal treatment within 3 months, acute/chronic somatic diseases or infections
Clinical assessment: Eating Disorder Inventory-3 (EDI-3) questionnaire used
FMT experiment: 6-week-old female germ-free Swiss Webster mice transplanted with stool from 3 AN-RS cases and 3 healthy controls
FMT diet protocol: 30% energy-restricted autoclaved chow diet for 3 weeks to mimic AN eating behavior
Metabolic measurements: fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, C-reactive protein
Genetic findings: 10-kbp deletion in B. uniformis associated with bulimia and self-denial; encodes thiamine-monophosphate kinase
Study design: Cross-sectional observational study with mechanistic follow-up in mice
Aggregate mortality of AN: 5.6% per decade
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: We performed shotgun metagenomics on faecal samples from 77 female AN cases and 70 age-matched female controls allowing for in-depth analyses of the gut bacterial and archaeal microbiota.
uncurated_metadata.section: Methods — Study participants and Main text
uncurated_metadata.notes: Metadata extracted from Methods section and results describing study design, participant characteristics, and key experimental protocols.

host_species.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females
host_species.notes: Primary study cohort consists of human female participants. Secondary experiments were conducted in female germ-free Swiss Webster mice (Mus musculus), but the primary biomarker study is in humans.

Sequencing_platform reflects shotgun metagenomics (Ion Proton); animal 16S rRNA experiments used IlluminaMiSeq but are secondary.
Age and age_unit are inferred (Adult/Year) from context rather than explicitly reported as study-level statistics.
DNA_extraction_kit field uses MACHEREY-NAGEL NucleoSpin, which does not exactly match allowed enum values; mapped to NorgenBiotek as closest equivalent.
NCBI accessions not mentioned in paper text; may be available in supplementary data or GEO/ENA but not extracted here.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('study_level'); kept batch 0.

Batch 1 subgroups ['AN (Anorexia Nervosa)', 'HC (Healthy Controls)', 'AN-RS (Anorexia Nervosa - Restricting Subtype)', 'AN-BP (Anorexia Nervosa - Binge/Purging Subtype)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Paper is primarily a study-level design (cohort study with AN cases and controls); no per-sample individual metadata table provided in supplementary materials.
FMT mouse experiments include animal subjects not humans; donor demographics reported but recipient mice data not mapped to schema.
Age range for study participants not explicitly stated; only EDI-3 validated age range (13–53 years) inferred.
Specific medication usage percentages/counts for AN cohort not reported; only used as statistical covariates.
Smoking history distribution not quantified in text despite being used as a covariate.
Recent antibiotic use was an exclusion criterion (within 3 months), but current use status for included participants not explicitly verified.

Schema fields `disease_response_os`, `ecog_performance_status`, and `tumor_size_measurement` are not applicable to this anorexia nervosa microbiome study. No survival, performance status, or oncology data are reported.

Biomarker values are reported as relative abundances, fold-changes, and association statistics (Cliff's delta, P-values) rather than absolute concentrations, making direct numerical value extraction difficult without reference to individual tables.

`feces_phenotype_value` captures qualitative phenotypic descriptions; quantitative measurements are distributed across figures (e.g., Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3, Fig. 6) rather than a single summary table.
The paper includes both human (n=147) and mouse (n=20) cohorts; extracted metadata pertains primarily to the human study unless otherwise specified.
